title: Genesis' two lights matched to the cosmic microwave background

tellings.quote: light returned to the universe and that's the light of the second day.

plain: Greg Rogers, a former NASA doctor, tells Michels that the lights in the opening of Genesis match the history of the early universe, and that the light of the second day is the moment "light returned to the universe," which he links to the cosmic microwave background, the faint afterglow of the early universe that fills space. He reads it from the King James Bible of 1611, where God says "Let there be light: and there was light," and that is "the first day." The text gives the order of creation; whether its days line up with the stages a physicist would name, it leaves to the reader, and Rogers's matching would mean the ancient account kept a memory of how the cosmos began.
